problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,d=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -11 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
.

activity_context.topic_title: Linear Combinations of Vectors in N-Dimensional Euclidean Space

examples.knowledge_point: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination
examples.problem:
Consider the vectors

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14082816/assets/cc8a77d53637f5523dcdadd79ea3a282efe30b96aaeb9ec31fce1f39d4006186.png)

If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2  = \mathbf d,$ then what is $x_1+x_2?$
examples.worked_solution:
If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2  = \mathbf d,$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=5 \\ -{x}_{1}=-5 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we obtain $x_1=5,$ which we substitute into the first equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =5 \\ 4(5)+{x}_{2} & =5 \\ {x}_{2} & =-15.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x_1=5$ and $x_2=-15$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =0 \\ 3(5)+(-15) & =0 \\ 0 & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is $x_1=5$ and $x_2=-15,$ which means

$$
5 \mathbf{c_1}-15 \mathbf{c_2} = \mathbf{d}.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_1+x_2=5-15=-10.
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the value of ${x}_{1}-{x}_{2}$ given that $7a+4x=b$ and

$$
a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4 \\ -3 \\ -6\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}7a+4x & =b \\ 4x & =b-7a \\ x & =\frac{1}{4}(b-7a) \\ x & =\frac{1}{4}([\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4 \\ -3 \\ -6\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]) \\ x & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 4 \\ 4 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\ x & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-2-1=-3.$
